item.title: [TIFF - Toronto Film Festival] CHRONOVISOR Trailer | TIFF
item.description:
The Chonovisor is a legendary, occult time-viewing device invented by an Italian Benedictine monk in the 1950s, who claimed to have witnessed the crucifixion of Christ through his machine that could visually capture and relay any moment in history through a television set. Chronovisor, the debut feature from filmmakers Kevin Walker and Jack Auen, is a docu-fiction hybrid that follows Béatrice (Anne-Laure Sellier), a respected academic, who risks her reputation as she becomes transfixed by this allegedly true story. Her obsession with researching the mythical machine takes her from her Upper East Side apartment to the hidden depths of New York’s libraries. This mystery has been compared to Umberto Eco’s The Name of the Rose and has been described by film critics as an “academic-noir.” Shot entirely on 16mm in warm low light, the film is also a remarkable formal exercise in scanning and capturing pages, translations, recordings, photographs, drawings, and videotapes. The film had its world premiere at Rotterdam and was selected to screen at New Directors/New Films. This is its Canadian Premiere.

item.title: [Netflix Anime] Sparks of Tomorrow | New Episodes Trailer | Netflix
item.description:
Dive headlong into new episodes of "Sparks of Tomorrow" and get closer to discovering the secrets hidden within the 20th Century Electric Catalog! Each person faces ordeals in a bid to bring their dreams to life.

In an alternate version of the early 20th century where technological progress evolved along a different path shaped by steam power, Kyoto is blanketed in constant smoke.
A boy, hardened by the loss of his brother, grows distrustful after their shared dream of an "Age of Electricity" is cut short.
A deeply devout girl hides her dreams and regrets for her deceased mother deep within her heart.
When the two cross paths, they set about exploring the secrets of the 20th Century Electrical Catalog, a glimpse into the future they long for.

In this tale of regeneration, they must confront their pasts together and carve a path toward the future they once believed in.

item.title: [Netflix Anime] Fool Night | Official Teaser #2 | Netflix
item.description:
Transfloration — a technology that implants seeds into the bodies of those near death, transforming them into plants. It is the desperate measure humanity has chosen to ensure its survival.

In a distant future where thick clouds cover the sky, trapping Earth in constant winter and night, most of the planet’s vegetation has withered away. Facing a serious oxygen shortage, humanity has built a society that relies on the meager amount of oxygen provided by Transfloration.

A young man, Toshiro Kamiya, lives in poverty and works hard to pay taxes, cover living expenses, and afford medication for his mentally ill mother. However, the cruel reality around him gradually eats away at his hope.

In their first collaboration, Sunrise and Shaft present “Fool Night,"
a highly anticipated anime adaptation of the globally acclaimed manga.
All episodes start streaming on Thursday, November 26, 2026, only on Netflix.

Koki Uchiyama as Toshiro Kamiya / Minako Kotobuki as Yomiko Horai

item.title: [TIFF - Toronto Film Festival] KEN RUSSELL'S THE DEVILS Trailer | TIFF 2026
item.description:
Ken Russell’s 1971 The Devils remains one of cinema’s most transgressive and incendiary provocations, a feverish account of the Loudun possessions witchcraft trial in 17th-century France. Oliver Reed stars as Urbain Grandier, a wildly charismatic libertine priest who defies Cardinal Richelieu’s consolidation of power. Vanessa Redgrave’s Sister Jeanne is a sexually repressed, hunchbacked Abbess obsessed with Grandier with an intensity that ignites accusations of demonic possession among her convent’s nuns. Already a target for reprisals due to his political resistance, Grandier’s promiscuity eventually lands him on the wrong side of a powerful family.

item.title: [Modern Films] Everybody Digs Bill Evans | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Winner of the Silver Bear for Best Director at the 2026 Berlin Film Festival, Everybody Digs Bill Evans is a biographical drama film about the legendary jazz pianist and composer Bill Evans.

Directed by Grant Gee and starring Anders Danielsen Lie, Bill Pullman and Laurie Metcalf, the film is written by Mark O’Halloran and based on Owen Martell’s novel Intermission.

1961. Bill Evans is playing with what he considers the perfect musical trio until tragedy strikes in the premature death of his bass player, Scott LaFaro - his musical soulmate. Traumatised by grief, Evans stops playing for the first time since his childhood. A tug-of-war between personal torment and the seemingly safer haven of familial love will see Evans oscillate between New York and suburbia, his genius always bubbling beneath the surface.

DIRECTOR Grant Gee
CAST Anders Danielsen Lie, Bill Pullman, Laurie Metcalf, Barry Ward, Valene Kane

In UK and Irish cinemas September 11

item.title: [Modern Films] Leonora in the Morning Light | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Defiant, brilliant, and untamable, Leonora Carrington refused to live by anyone’s rules but her own. In the charged atmosphere of 1930s Paris, she falls under the spell of the Surrealist movement—and into a passionate, volatile love affair with the German artist Max Ernst. Together, they create a world where art and life blur, surrounded by icons like André Breton and Salvador Dalí, and build an otherworldly refuge in the south of France filled with sculpted creatures and strange, living dreams.

But as war engulfs Europe, their fantasy shatters. Ernst is arrested as an enemy alien, and Leonora is thrust into a nightmare of loss, madness, and survival. Fleeing to Spain, she spirals into psychological torment and endures brutal institutional treatment. Emerging scarred but unbroken, Leonora finds her way to Mexico—a place of magic and rebirth—where she reclaims her art, her identity, and her freedom.

Leonora in the Morning Light is the epic true story of a woman who turned trauma into transcendence, creating beauty from chaos and forging a legacy that changed the history of modern art.

DIRECTOR Thor Klein & Lena Vurma
CAST Olivia Vinall, Alexander Scheer, Cassandra Ciangherotti, Ryan Gage, Istvan Teglas, Luis Gerardo Mendez

In UK and Irish cinemas May 29

item.description:
A Venice Film Festival World Premiere, Neo Sora’s striking debut feature is set in a dystopian near-future Tokyo, where teenagers rebel against societal expectations. The film offers a vivid coming-of-age portrait, following best friends Yuta and Kou as they confront a world where AI surveillance is tightening under the yoke of oppressive authoritarianism. item.title: [Modern Films] Oslo Stories Trilogy: Sex | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Premiered in Berlinale’s Panorama, Sex follows two men, both in heterosexual marriages, who have an unexpected experience that challenges their understanding of sexuality, gender, and identity. One has a sexual encounter with another man, without considering it either as an expression of homosexuality or infidelity, and discusses it with his wife afterwards. The other finds himself in nocturnal dreams where he is seen as a woman, stirring confusion and leading him to question how much his personality is shaped by the gaze of others.

Part of the OSLO STORIES TRILOGY: DREAMS LOVE SEX from director Dag Johan Haugerud.

CAST Gunnar Røise, Thorbjørn Harr, Siri Forberg, Birgitte Larsen

In UK and Irish cinemas August 22

item.title: [Modern Films] Oslo Stories Trilogy: Love | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Premiered in Competition at the Venice Film Festival, Love follows Marianne, a pragmatic doctor, and Tor, a compassionate nurse, who are both avoiding conventional relationships. One evening, after a blind date, Marianne encounters Tor on the ferry. Tor, who often spends his nights there seeking casual encounters with men, shares his experiences of spontaneous intimacy. Intrigued by his perspective, Marianne begins to explore whether casual intimacy could also be an option for her.

Part of the OSLO STORIES TRILOGY: DREAMS LOVE SEX from director Dag Johan Haugerud.

CAST Andrea Bræin Hovig, Tayo Cittadella Jacobsen, Marte Engebrigtsen, Lars Jacob Holm, Thomas Gullestad, Marian Saastad Ottesen, Morten Svartveit

item.title: [Modern Films] Oslo Stories Trilogy: Dreams | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
Winner of the Golden Bear at the 2025 Berlin Film Festival, DREAMS follows Johanne as she falls in love for the first time, with her teacher. To preserve her feelings, she documents her emotions and experiences in writing. When her mother and grandmother read what she has written, they are initially shocked by its intimate content but soon see that it has literary potential. As they debate whether to publish it, Johanne navigates the gap between her romantic fantasy and reality, and all three women confront their differing views on love, sexuality, and self-discovery.

Part of the OSLO STORIES TRILOGY: DREAMS LOVE SEX from director Dag Johan Haugerud.

item.title: [Modern Films] E.1027 - Eileen Gray And The House By The Sea | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
A love triangle of jealousy in the Parisian art scene of the 1930s is brought to life in a stylish docufiction about iconic artist and architect Eileen Gray, who built her modernist dream house on the Riviera, only to be upstaged by Le Corbusier.

Eileen Gray had a truly eminent sense of design. The Irish artist and architect created some of the most iconic furniture of the 20th century, so when she focussed her unique artistic vision on developing a house for herself on the Riviera in 1929, the result was a modernist triumph. A house and a work of art in one, overlooking the sun-sparkled infinity of the Mediterranean. The house is named E.1027, a cryptic contraction of the names of Gray and her lover, Romanian architect Jean Badovici. But when the Swiss-French star architect Le Corbusier learns of the house, he becomes obsessed – perhaps because Gray breathes light, air and soul into her building, which is not just a machine to live in.

‘E.1027 – Eileen Gray and the House by the Sea’ reconstructs the dramatic story of Gray and the house that Le Corbusier amazingly managed to convince the world he had built himself. A stunningly beautiful and cinematic docufiction where the inspiration from Gray is present in lines, colours and shapes – but where they serve the narrative of a brilliant female artist who spent a long life in the shadow of her male colleagues.

In UK and Irish cinemas May 16
https://www.modernfilms.com/e1027

item.title: [Modern Films] Blue Road: The Edna O'Brien Story | Official UK Trailer
item.description:
In 1960, a young Irish woman named Edna O’Brien wrote a sexually frank debut novel, The Country Girls. She became a literary sensation, writing for The New Yorker, delivering provocative interviews, and authoring screenplays.

Her success enraged her writer husband and made her a pariah in her native Ireland, where her books were banned and burned. She would make her home in London, where she conducted numerous love affairs, hosted star-studded parties, and made and lost a fortune.

In July 2024, Edna passed away and this film provides a final testimony from her, aged 93, as she reflects upon her extraordinary life for filmmaker Sinéad O’Shea’s camera.

Granting the director access to her personal journals — read aloud in the film by the Oscar nominated Irish actress Jessie Buckley — and with additional perspectives offered from Gabriel Byrne, Walter Mosley and an array of renowned writers, Edna does not shy from any subject.

Blue Road is as candid, dark, and enchanting as O’Brien’s wonderful novels.

In UK cinemas April 18
https://www.modernfilms.com/blueroad

item.title: [Modern Films] The Return | Official UK Trailer | Starring Ralph Fiennes and Juliette Binoche
item.description:
The Return tells the story of the mythical Greek hero, Odysseus (Fiennes) who, after 20 years away, washes up on the shores of Ithaca, haggard and unrecognisable. The King has returned from the Trojan War, but much has changed in his kingdom. His beloved wife Penelope (Binoche) is a prisoner in her own home, hounded by suitors vying to be king and planning the death of Telemachus, the son he never knew. Shattered by his experience of war, Odysseus must rediscover his strength in order to win back all that he has lost.

Join us for a special preview of The Return, starring Ralph Fiennes and Juliette Binoche, directed by Uberto Pasolini. The screening on 9 April will be followed by a discussion, broadcast live from the British Museum, with Academy Award nominee Ralph Fiennes, British Museum's Keeper of Greece and Rome, Tom Harrison, and Curator: Reception of the Ancient Mediterranean, Vicky Donnellan. Find out more about a broadcast near you at modernfilms.com/thereturn or see your local cinema for more details.

A film by Uberto Pasolini
Starring Ralph Fiennes, Juliette Binoche, Charlie Plummer, Marwan Kenzari, Claudio Santamaria and Ángela Molina

In UK and Irish cinemas April 11
https://www.modernfilms.com/thereturn
